needsHuman.title: Volt-Var Smart Inverter Control to Eliminate Overvoltage Disconnections at 300 Solar Sites
needsHuman.markdown:
## Volt-Var Smart Inverter Control to Eliminate Overvoltage Disconnections at 300 Solar Sites

**Company:** Described problem works in solar energy. [C999] Challenge C999-CH1.  
**Researcher:** Aleksandar Jeremić is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R0696]  
**Format:** joint project, one page.

### The problem
Rooftop solar inverters at 300 sites disconnect from the grid on hot summer afternoons when local grid voltage rises too high, and the company has tried lowering the export limit to address this. [C999-CH1] The company's current workaround — reducing the export limit — recovers grid connectivity but costs approximately 8% of yearly energy yield across the portfolio. [C999-CH1] The company holds five years of inverter logs and grid voltage readings from 300 sites. [C999-CH1]

### Prior work
- A 2021 study compared four reactive power control techniques for solar PV inverters in a low-voltage network and found that incorporating reactive power controls of solar PV inverters aids in successfully mitigating overvoltage issues. [W3177274304]

### Research questions
1. Can a Volt-Var or droop-based reactive power control strategy, parameterised from the five-year inverter and voltage log dataset, prevent inverter disconnections at peak-generation hours — measured as the number of disconnection events in a held-out summer season reduced to zero, with no reduction in active power export relative to the uncurtailed baseline?
2. Which feeder segments and site clusters drive the majority of overvoltage events — measured by hosting capacity analysis against the 300-site voltage logs, producing a ranked map of congestion severity?
3. Does a two-stage control scheme (day-ahead Volt-Var scheduling plus real-time droop correction) outperform a fixed power-factor strategy on the same feeders — measured by peak voltage exceedance margin and reactive power losses across the simulated summer period?

### Approach
- Parse and quality-screen five years of inverter logs and grid voltage readings from 300 sites; reconstruct feeder topology and load/generation time series to build a validated steady-state power-flow model using backward–forward sweep analysis as in the researcher's feeder studies.
- Apply probabilistic hosting capacity assessment — using stochastic simulation and feeder classification — to rank the 300 sites by overvoltage contribution and identify the feeders where reactive power headroom is sufficient to substitute for active power curtailment.
- Design Volt-Var control curves and a two-stage reactive power coordination scheme (day-ahead scheduling with real-time droop correction) calibrated to the identified feeders; validate the design against the five-year dataset using time-series power-flow simulation, targeting zero disconnection events with no export reduction.
- Test the preferred control parameterisation in a hardware-in-the-loop environment using the researcher's real-time digital simulator to confirm dynamic stability before the company configures inverters in the field.

### Plan

| Period | Work | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Months 1–3 | A master's student from the researcher's group, supported by the company's engineer (30% time), parses the five-year log dataset, reconstructs feeder topologies, and builds a validated power-flow model for the ten worst-performing sites. Jeremić supervises model setup and data validation. | Validated feeder models for ten sites; ranked map of overvoltage severity across 300 sites; data-quality report. |
| Months 4–6 | Hosting capacity assessment extended to all 300 sites using stochastic simulation; reactive power headroom quantified per feeder. Volt-Var control curves and two-stage coordination parameters designed and tested in time-series power-flow simulation against the five-year dataset. | Control parameter set that eliminates simulated disconnections with no active power curtailment; comparison report against fixed power-factor baseline. |
| Months 7–9 | Preferred control scheme validated on the real-time digital simulator using hardware-in-the-loop testing. Company engineer integrates the validated parameters into inverter configuration files for a pilot group of sites. | Hardware-in-the-loop validation report; inverter configuration files ready for field pilot; one journal or conference paper submitted. |

### First six months
- Week 1–2: the company transfers five years of inverter logs and voltage readings (anonymised per data-sharing agreement) to a secure repository accessible to the researcher's group; the company's engineer provides feeder topology diagrams for the 20 sites with the most recorded disconnections.
- Month 1: the master's student sets up the power-flow modelling environment and runs a data-quality audit; disconnection events are extracted and linked to voltage exceedance timestamps across all 300 sites.
- Months 2–3: feeder models for the ten highest-severity sites are built and validated against historical voltage readings; hosting capacity is assessed for these sites and results reviewed jointly by Jeremić and the company's engineer.
- Months 4–6: stochastic hosting capacity assessment scales to all 300 sites; Volt-Var control curves are designed and first time-series simulations run; interim results presented to the company with a go/no-go recommendation on the control approach before hardware-in-the-loop work begins.

### What each side brings
- **Company:** Five years of inverter logs and grid voltage readings from 300 sites, held by the company. [C999-CH1]
- **Faculty:** Jeremić co-authored hosting capacity assessment and probabilistic mapping methods for low-voltage distribution networks using stochastic simulation and feeder classification. [SYN-PUB-07801, SYN-PUB-07799, SYN-PUB-07796] Jeremić co-authored smart inverter Volt-Var control design and hardware-in-the-loop testing with a real-time digital simulator for distributed voltage regulation. [SYN-PUB-07797] Jeremić co-authored a two-stage reactive power coordination framework combining day-ahead scheduling with real-time rule-based droop correction. [SYN-PUB-03969] Jeremić has access to real-time digital simulator hardware and field measurement equipment, and can facilitate data-sharing agreements with a regional distribution system operator for validation against real feeder topologies. [R0696]

### Why this pair
The company brings five years of multi-site operational data from 300 sites; Jeremić brings the hosting capacity methodology and hardware-in-the-loop testing capability needed to turn that data into a validated control design. Jeremić brings the published Volt-Var and reactive power coordination methods and the real-time digital simulator needed to validate the design before field deployment; the company brings the operational dataset from 300 sites and the inverter fleet on which the validated design would run. Together they can close the loop from diagnosis to field-ready configuration within nine months.

- The company has five years of inverter logs and grid voltage readings from 300 sites and a quantified yield cost of 8% from the current export-limit workaround. [C999-CH1]
- Jeremić co-authored Volt-Var control design and hardware-in-the-loop testing methods and two-stage reactive power coordination targeting overvoltage in low-voltage distribution networks. [SYN-PUB-07797, SYN-PUB-03969]
- Jeremić performed consultancy with Elektrovojvodina d.o.o. on distributed generation connection evaluation, demonstrating prior engagement with Serbian distribution grid practice. [R0696]

### Risks and constraints
- The records cover feeder-level simulation and hosting capacity methodology; whether the five-year multi-site log dataset from 300 sites requires additional data-engineering work not covered by the existing publications is not stated. [SYN-PUB-07801, SYN-PUB-07799, C999-CH1]
- The steady-state power flow and Volt-Var work covers LV feeder analysis, but the records do not describe experience with proprietary inverter log formats or data integration pipelines at the scale of 300 sites (SYN-PUB-07794, SYN-PUB-07797). [SYN-PUB-07794, SYN-PUB-07797]

### Agreed up front (proposed)
- Publication: the researcher's group may submit findings for publication after a 45-day review period during which the company may request removal of commercially sensitive feeder or site details.
- Ownership: the company owns the inverter configuration files, calibrated control parameters, and field pilot results; the University of Novi Sad retains the right to use the methodology and anonymised simulation results for further research and teaching.
- Data access: the company provides the five-year log dataset under a data-sharing agreement signed before work begins; the dataset is stored on infrastructure accessible only to named project members and is deleted or returned at project end.
- Preconditions: the data-sharing agreement and any required consent from the regional distribution system operator must be in place before the master's student begins data processing in Month 1.

### Sources
- C999: Described problem
- C999-CH1: Our rooftop solar inverters disconnect from the grid on hot summer afternoons because the local grid voltage rises to...
- R0696: Aleksandar Jeremić
- SYN-PUB-03969: Coordinated Reactive Power Dispatch in Low-Voltage Networks Using a Two-Stage Optimisation Framework (2022)
- SYN-PUB-07794: Steady-State Voltage Profile Analysis in Radial Low-Voltage Feeders with Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems (2013)
- SYN-PUB-07796: Hosting Capacity Assessment for Photovoltaic Systems in Low-Voltage Urban Networks: Deterministic and Stochastic Appr... (2018)
- SYN-PUB-07797: Smart Inverter Volt–Var Control for Voltage Regulation in Prosumer-Integrated Low-Voltage Feeders (2020)
- SYN-PUB-07799: Feeder Reconfiguration as a Hosting Capacity Enhancement Tool in Meshed Low-Voltage Networks (2023)
- SYN-PUB-07801: Probabilistic Hosting Capacity Maps for Low-Voltage Distribution Networks: A Methodology for Municipal-Scale Assessment (2025)
- W3177274304: Comparison of Reactive Power Control Techniques for Solar PV Inverters to Mitigate Voltage Rise in Low-Voltage Grids (2021) https://openalex.org/W3177274304

claim.text: Rooftop solar inverters at 300 sites disconnect from the grid on hot summer afternoons when local grid voltage exceeds the inverter's limit. Lowering the export limit to prevent disconnections reduces yearly yield by about 8%. The company has five years of inverter logs and grid voltage readings from 300 sites (C999-CH1).

rejected.reason: The source states disconnection occurs because 'local grid voltage rises too high,' not because it 'exceeds the inverter's limit' — that characterisation is added by the claim and is not in C999-CH1.

claim.text: Lowering the export limit to prevent disconnections reduces yearly yield by about 8%, indicating that a solution must maintain generation while respecting grid voltage limits (C999-CH1).

rejected.reason: C999-CH1 states the ~8% yield loss fact, but the conclusion that 'a solution must maintain generation while respecting grid voltage limits' is a judgement/inference not present in the cited text.

claim.text: Cycle-ageing modelling and degradation quantification for lithium-ion and lead-acid batteries using rainflow-counting and Arrhenius methods.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-03706 covers rainflow-counting degradation for lithium-ion cells; SYN-PUB-03710 covers Arrhenius-based temperature-dependent degradation; however, neither cited source mentions lead-acid batteries, and SYN-PUB-03709 mentions rainflow-based damage accumulation and reviews ageing models but does not specifically cover lead-acid degradation quantification with rainflow-counting or Arrhenius methods.

claim.text: Coordinated scheduling of electric vehicle charging and flexible residential loads under dynamic tariffs using model predictive control and distributed optimization.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-06208 covers distributed MPC for coordinated EV charging; SYN-PUB-06210 covers joint scheduling of heat pumps and EV chargers under dynamic tariffs using MILP (not MPC or distributed optimization); SYN-PUB-06206 covers day-ahead optimal EV charging under real-time pricing using MIQP—neither SYN-PUB-06210 nor SYN-PUB-06206 use model predictive control or distributed optimization, so the claim overstates the methods across all three papers.

claim.text: Aggregation of residential flexible loads into equivalent virtual battery models for demand response portfolio management.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-06207 describes deriving virtual battery parameters for EV chargers, heat pumps, and washing machines and validating the model for a 500-household portfolio, but the claim adds 'demand response portfolio management' which is not explicitly stated in that record—the record describes the virtual battery abstraction and a receding-horizon control demonstration, not specifically 'portfolio management'.

claim.text: Metaheuristic approaches—genetic algorithm, differential evolution, particle swarm optimization—for large-scale demand response scheduling.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-06148 covers genetic algorithm, differential evolution, and particle swarm optimization (as well as simulated annealing) for large-scale demand response scheduling, but SYN-PRJ-0695 (ADRIAFLEX) does not mention metaheuristic approaches; the claim attributes the metaheuristic topic partly to SYN-PRJ-0695, which does not contain that fact.

claim.text: Maintains access to real-time digital simulator hardware, field measurement equipment, and established data-sharing relationship with regional distribution system operator for validation of products against real feeder topologies and smart meter data.

rejected.reason: R0696 states the group uses RTDS real-time digital simulator hardware and maintains access to field measurement equipment, and that Jeremić has an established working relationship with Elektrovojvodina d.o.o. and can facilitate data-sharing agreements for companies requiring real feeder topology or smart meter data for product validation — however, the claim says 'established data-sharing relationship' whereas R0696 says he 'can facilitate data-sharing agreements', meaning no such relationship currently exists; the text describes the ability to facilitate agreements, not an established data-sharing relationship.

claim.text: Virtual battery aggregation models for residential flexible loads including EV chargers, heat pumps, and washing machines.

rejected.reason: "EV" is not in SYN-PUB-06207 but is in SYN-PUB-06208, SYN-PUB-04229, SYN-PUB-06212, SYN-PUB-06213, SYN-PUB-06214, R0530 and SYN-PRJ-0694, which the claim does not cite.

claim.text: Anomaly detection in industrial SCADA telemetry using isolation forest, autoencoders, and LSTM architectures on real-world data from PV parks, wind farms, and district heating systems.

rejected.reason: "LSTM" is not in SYN-PUB-08188, SYN-PUB-08187, SYN-PUB-08186 or SYN-PUB-08183 but is in SYN-PUB-08184, which the claim does not cite.

claim.text: Predictive maintenance scheduling using survival analysis, gradient-boosted trees, and random forests on vibration and SCADA data to estimate remaining useful life and rank maintenance priorities.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-08184 uses LSTM (not gradient-boosted trees or random forests) for RUL prediction, and SYN-PUB-08182 uses random forest for fault classification (not RUL estimation or maintenance scheduling), so the claim's assertion that gradient-boosted trees and random forests are used to estimate remaining useful life is not supported by the cited texts.

claim.text: Fault detection and classification in photovoltaic inverters and string arrays using feature extraction, transfer learning across sites, and domain adaptation with small labelled samples.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-08185 does not use the term 'domain adaptation' — it describes feature alignment via quantile normalisation for cross-site transfer — and neither cited source explicitly mentions 'string arrays' as a target (SYN-PUB-08182 covers string inverters, not string arrays), so the claim adds terms not found in the cited texts.

claim.text: Provided six-month consultancy to a regional solar asset management company during 2022–2023 on specification and implementation of automated performance reporting systems.

rejected.reason: R0738 states the consultancy involved 'partial implementation' of the automated performance reporting system, whereas the claim states 'implementation' without 'partial', overstating what the record says.

claim.text: Predictive maintenance scheduling using gradient-boosted survival models on vibration and SCADA data to estimate remaining useful life and rank maintenance priorities.

rejected.reason: SYN-PUB-02957 describes gradient-boosted survival models on vibration and SCADA data used to estimate failure probability and generate ranked maintenance schedules, but the claim states 'remaining useful life' whereas the paper estimates '30-day failure probability' and uses a 'discrete-time hazard model' — remaining useful life is not mentioned in the cited text.
